newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK VW SEES '97 OUTPUT STEADY WITH '96.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK VW SEES '97 OUTPUT STEADY WITH '96.

text.p: Volkswagen Bratislava s.r.o., the Slovak subsidiary of German car maker Volkswagen AG, plans to keep output at 30,000 cars in 1997, after producing 30,147 cars in 1996, a Slovak VW official said.
"Production in 1996, worth about 18 billion crowns in total, had exceeded our original plans by 5,147 cars," VW manager Jaroslav Holecek told Reuters on Tuesday.
Holecek said the plant had exceeded estimates also in the production of gear-boxes and components, with investments totalling some 750 million crowns, provided by its German parent company.
He said results for 1996 were expected to be released after international audits in February and March.
He would not elaborate on investment plans for 1997, saying these had yet to be officially aproved.
In 1996, Slovak VW assembled 5,156 units of the Golf A3 Syncro model, 5,681 Golf Variant Syncro, 3,421 Passats and 15,889 units of the Golf A3.
"We assembled our last Passat in August, therefore our entire production will constist only of Golf and Golf Syncro models this year," Holecek said.
VW made 259,646 gear boxes and 5.8 million components in 1996, after 186,400 gear boxes and 1.76 million components in the previous year.
"We expect to increase our production by 10,000 gear boxes and by a million components in 1997," Holecek added.
Volkswagen AG originally took a stake in Bratislavske Automobilove Zavody (BAZ) in 1992, and became its sole owner acquiring the remaining 20 percent shares of BAZ in December 1995.
VW Bratislava employs some 950 people to assemble cars from kits imported from Germany. Volkswagen investment into the Slovak plant between 1992 and 1994 totalled 130 million marks.
The factory, which has a capacity to build some 30,000 cars of various models a year, exports roughly 95 percent of its production, mainly to western Europe.
Last May, VW started production at its second plant in Slovakia, making car cabling systems in Nitra, 90 km east of Bratislava.
The venture, Volkswagen Elektricke Systemy s.r.o. supplies car cabling systems to VW group plants as well as to other car maufacturers.
